﻿Notes

XML
In Visual Programming (VP), XML (Extensible Markup Language)is used to visually design structured data, like making digital forms, organizing information, or creating configurations. VP tools help you work with XML without writing code, making things like data organization and sharing easier.
Imagine you're using a VP tool to create a recipe app. You visually design the layout of each recipe page, including elements like ingredients, cooking steps, and images. The VP tool generates XML code behind the scenes to represent the structure of each recipe. When users interact with your app, they see the visual layout you designed, but the app reads and processes the underlying XML data to display recipes consistently. This way, you're designing the app visually while utilizing XML for data representation.
WPF (Windows Presentation Foundation)
In Visual Programming (VP), WPF (Windows Presentation Foundation) is used for designing attractive desktop app interfaces. VP tools make it easy by letting you visually create WPF UI elements, arrange layouts, handle events, and connect data without extensive coding.
"Extensive coding" means writing a lot of complex and detailed programming instructions to achieve a specific task or feature in an application.
Grid Length
In Visual Programming, "Grid Length" specifies how rows or columns in a layout grid should size – fixed pixels, proportions, or content-based. It helps create flexible and responsive designs without writing code..
Grand Central Dispatch
In Visual Programming, "Grand Central Dispatch" (GCD) is like a helper that allows you to do multiple tasks at the same time in a smooth way. It ensures your app stays responsive and doesn't get stuck when handling different tasks together. It's useful for managing tasks without making your app slow or unresponsive.
jQuery
In Visual Programming (VP), jQuery simplifies web development. It helps manage user interactions, modify webpage content, and add visual effects visually, without in-depth coding.
Objective-C
In Visual Programming (VP), Objective-C is used for designing and implementing Apple apps. VP tools help create app interfaces and logic visually, while Objective-C handles the behind-the-scenes functionality.
In Visual Programming (VP), Objective-C is used when creating applications for Apple devices like iPhones, iPads, and Mac computers. VP tools make it possible to visually design user interfaces and interactions, while Objective-C is used to implement the functionality of these interfaces and manage the app's behavior. It's commonly used in mobile app development and macOS application development.
Differentiate the need of Binding and Command in WPF. in vp
Binding connects UI and data to keep them in sync.
Command handles user interactions and associated actions, promoting cleaner separation of logic.
In VP tools, you visually set up both for effective UI design and user interaction.
Automatic Looping in jQuery (VP) difference Chaining Functions in jQuery (VP):
Performing actions on multiple elements without manual loops. For example, hiding all paragraphs with $("p").hide();.
Chaining Functions in jQuery (VP):
Applying multiple actions to the same elements in one line. For instance, $("p").hide().fadeIn(); hides and then fades in paragraphs. In VP, it simplifies element manipulation.
How to localize binary resource.
Localizing binary resources in visual programming means making your program friendly and usable for people who speak different languages. To do this, you separate the pictures and other non-text things in your program and create special files for each language to hold the translations. Then, your program can choose the right pictures and resources based on the language the user prefers. Finally, you test everything to make sure it works properly for all languages you support.
binary resources are categorized into:
Executable Binary Resources: These contain code for tasks and programs.
Non-Executable Binary Resources: These hold data like images, audio, and config files.
Ajax is interaction of which type of technologies?
JavaScript: JavaScript is used to make asynchronous requests to the server and handle the response without requiring a page refresh. It enables dynamic updates and interaction on web pages.
XMLHttpRequest (XmlHttp): XmlHttp is a JavaScript object that facilitates sending and receiving data between the web browser and the server asynchronously. It's a core component of Ajax, allowing data to be exchanged without disrupting the user's experience.

What are the 2 problems of memory management in IOs? in vp
Memory Leaks: Memory leaks occur when allocated memory is not properly deallocated or released after its intended use. This leads to memory being consumed unnecessarily over time, which can eventually degrade the performance of the app and even lead to crashes. Effective memory management techniques, such as using Automatic Reference Counting (ARC) in iOS, are crucial to prevent memory leaks.
Dangling Pointers: Dangling pointers refer to pointers that point to memory locations that have been deallocated or freed. Accessing such pointers can lead to unpredictable behavior and crashes. 1. Suppose if a user touched the Iphone screen three times separately like after one another, in
   the scenario what will be the status of TouchBegan?

       A.   Three UITouch events in a set
       B.   One UITouch event in a set Correct
       C.   Multiple UITouch eventss in a multiple set
       D.   One TouchBegan with 2 Sets

       Note:

                 If a user touched the iPhone screen three times separately, with each touch event
                 occurring after the previous one had ended, then the status of TouchBegan will be
                 "One UITouch event in a set."

                 In iOS development, the touchesBegan(_:with:) method is called when one or more
                 fingers touch the screen. When multiple fingers touch the screen, each touch is
                 represented by a separate UITouch object. However, if the user lifts their finger
                 from the screen and then touches it again, a new UITouch object is created for the
                 new touch event.

                 In the scenario you described, each touch event occurred after the previous one had
                 ended, so each touch event would result in a single UITouch object being created.
                 Therefore, the status of TouchBegan would be "One UITouch event in a set."

C++
C++ is the most preferred language for game development because of its capabilities to support
a variety of coding styles. C++ gives game programmers better control to manage the entire

applications and system programming including C++ game development.

of being lightweight comparatively. C++ code is faster than C# code; therefore, C++ has become
a preferred choice of game developers.

Python
The most popular library that supports developing games in Python is PyGame. This engine,
available under the LGPL, allows you to build fully commercial projects. What’s more, the
library is designed in a way that lets you easily use multiple processor cores. The main functions
were written in C and Assembler, thanks to which your project will be 10–20 times faster than if
it were written in Python only.
Another advantage of PyGame is that it works on any operating system, from Windows to the
Dreamcast console. All you need to do to start your adventure with PyGame is have Python 3
installed and run python3 -m pip install -U pygame --user in the environment. When the
package is installed, you can immediately start working on your game.

list of guides that are, in their opinion, worth your attention. You can find them here.

you to the intricacies of issues such as “Game Loop,” “Event,” or drawing in the game world.

C# is a simple, modern, object-oriented, and type-safe programming language, and it's the most
popular programming language in game development.

learn. C# is a high-level, general-purpose programming language that is easy to read because of
its well-defined class hierarchy. It is the perfect language for beginner developers as it will be
straightforward to grasp compared to most other languages.

Here are some suggestions for the different components of the application:

1. **Server-Side Processing**: For the server-side processing, a language like Java or C# would be a good choice. Both languages offer strong performance, scalability, and a wide range of libraries and frameworks for web development. These languages also have robust security features and support encryption mechanisms.

2. **Real-Time Data Updates**: For real-time data updates, you could consider using a technology like WebSocket, which provides full-duplex communication channels over a single TCP connection. WebSocket enables real-time data streaming and bi-directional communication between the server and the client, allowing for efficient and immediate updates.

3. **Integration Systems**: To integrate with external systems, you could leverage technologies such as RESTful APIs or messaging queues. RESTful APIs provide a standardized approach for communication between different systems, while messaging queues (e.g., RabbitMQ or Apache Kafka) allow asynchronous and reliable communication between components.

4. **Encryption and Security**: Ensuring encryption and security for financial transactions is crucial. You can utilize SSL/TLS protocols for secure communication over the network. Additionally, implementing secure coding practices, input validation, and access controls are important to protect sensitive data. Frameworks like Spring Security or ASP.NET Identity can provide authentication and authorization mechanisms.

5. **Front-End Development**: For the web-based user interface, you can use modern front-end frameworks like React or Angular. These frameworks offer a rich set of tools and libraries for building responsive and interactive user interfaces. They also have built-in security features and support for data encryption.

It's worth noting that the choice of programming languages and technologies may also depend on the existing infrastructure, development team expertise, and any specific requirements or regulations in the banking sector. Question 1: Which library is used to perform file input and output functions in C++?

A) #include<iostream>
B) #include<file.I/O>
C) #include<conio.h>
D) #include<fstream>

Correct Answer: D) #include<fstream>

Question 2: What is not a defense against patents and clean room design?

A) Event Invention
B) Dependent Invention
C) Clear Room Design
D) Independent Invention

Correct Answer: A) Event Invention

Question 3: The code given below is equivalent to _________.
<SolidColorBrush>White</SolidColorBrush>

Select the correct option:

A) <Brush Color="White">
B) <Brush Style="SolidWhite">
C) <SolidColorBrush Color="White"/>
D) <WhiteBrush>MyWhiteBrush</WhiteBrush>

Correct Answer: C) <SolidColorBrush Color="White"/>

Question 4: Which of the following access specifiers can be used for an interface in C#?

A) Protected
B) Private
C) Public
D) Internal

Correct Answer: C) Public

Question 5: In which type does the enumerators are stored by the compiler?

A) float
B) char
C) string
D) integer

Correct Answer: D) integer

Question 6: Which of the following doesn’t have Graphical User Interfaces and the Event-Driven
Model?

A) Web Applications
B) Desktop Applications
C) Mobile applications
D) Console Applications

Correct Answer: D) Console Applications

Question 7: To perform I/O operations, we must use _____ header file.

A) <ifstream>
B) <conio>
C) <fstream>
D) <ofstream>

Correct Answer: C) <fstream>

Question 8: Which of the following is an entity that introduces an event into the system?

A) Event Producer
B) Event Stream
C) Event Channel
D) Event Consumer

Correct Answer: A) Event Producer

Question 9: In C#, all binary operators are _________.

A) Left-associative
B) Top-associative
C) Center-associative
D) Right-associative

Correct Answer: A) Left-associative

A) Web Browser
B) Pressing a button
C) Swiping a credit card
D) E-Commerce site

Correct Answer: D) E-Commerce site

mouse enters it. In the C# code, the button is declared as Button b = sender as
Button;. What will be the correct way to change the foreground color of the button in
the event handler Button_mouseenter according to the specified requirements?

Options: a) b = color.black;
b) b.Foreground = Brushes.Black;
c) b.color = black;
d) color = b.black;

Answer: b) b.Foreground = Brushes.Black;

Question: ________ is the subclass of grid used to freeze some rows and columns of the
grid. Select the correct option.

Options: a) Wrap Grid
b) Selective Panel
c) Grid Panel
d) Selective Scrolling Grid

Answer: d) Selective Scrolling Grid

a) Add_Owner(Type, PropertyMetadata)
b) Owner(Type, PropertyMetadata)
c) AddOwner(Type, PropertyMetadata)
d) Owner_Add(Type, PropertyMetadata)

Answer: c) AddOwner(Type, PropertyMetadata)

a) Short memory
b) Grid
c) Indexing
d) Content Overflow

b) Freezable

1). Commands are a more robust and loosely coupled version of:
 Events

2). WPF defines a number of
 Built-in Commands

 Implementing icommand

4). icommand includes:
 Execute
 CanExecute
 CanExecuteChanged

5). For cut, copy and paste we can define and implement three classes mplementing
 icommand

6).Pre-defined Built-in Commands:
 Application Commands
 Component Commands
 Media Commands
 Navigation commands
 Editing Commands

8). Custom Commands don’t get the treatment of CommandConverter.

9). You can add KeyBinding and MouseBinding yourself.

                              www.vuanswer.com

    <KeyBinding Command = “NotaCommand” Key = “F1”> </Windows.InputBindings>

    KeyGesture(Key.F1)));

 win32 window

2). Any Number of child windows can be made by
 instantiating a window derived class and calling show

3). Child windows gets closed or minimized:
 on closing or minimizing of parent window

4). Window Events include:
 Activated
 Deactivated

5).Using Window.Show() a window appears and then disappears

6). StartupUri in xaml is
<Application x:Class = “PhotoGallery.App”
xmlns = http://schemas.microsoft.com.winfx/2006/xaml/presentation
xmlns: x = http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml
StartupUri = “MainWindow.xaml”/>

7). main() is created dynamically

8). System.Environment.GetCommandLineArgs is used to get command line
    arguments in WPF

9). Application Level Events are:
 Startup
 Exit
 Activated
 Deactivated
 SessionEnding

                                www.vuanswer.com

                               www.vuanswer.com
10). Window.show() is used to instantiate (Read-only) window.

11). Properties Dictionary is a simple Dictionary used to share things among different
    windows.

12). Application.Current() is used to take current window from any app.

13). Dispatcher.Run() is used to make multiple UI threads.

14). Single Instance App:
   Bool mutexIsNew;
using (System.Threading.Mutex m = New System.Threading.Mutex(True, uniqueName, out
    mutexIsNew))
    {
          if(mutexIsNew)
          // This is the first instance. Run the application
          else
          // There is already an instance running
}
15). Dialogs are just child windows

16).There are two types of dialogs:
 Modal
 Modeless

17). Modeless Dialog are more like normal Windows.

18). Modal Dialog are such windows that are necessary to terminate explicitly in order
    to interact with main window.

19). In modeless Window we can work in parallel with main window just like using
    Tools window in Photoshop.

20).Common Dialogs are actually provided by win32 and are part of Modal dialog.
21). Custom Dialogs are user-defined.

22). ShowDialog() returns us Null-able Boolean with options True/False/Null.

 Installation From CD

to develop device independent graphics so that same application/ GUI have same aspect
ratio and appearance on all kind of displays. e.g. Windows phone, Windows PC etc.

The length converter type converter associated with various length properties supports
specifying explicit units of cm, pt, in, or px (the default). Default are device independent
pixels. These logical pixels are 1/96 in regardless of screen DPI setting. They are always
stored as “double”. A typical display is 96 DPI.

5 marks) Name five builtin transform with default values

RotateTransform
RotateTransform, demonstrated in the preceding section, rotates an element according to
the values of three double properties:
. Angle—Angle of rotation, specified in degrees (default value = 0)
. CenterX—Horizontal center of rotation (default value = 0)
. CenterY—Vertical center of rotation (default value = 0)

ScaleTransform
ScaleTransform enlarges or shrinks an element horizontally, vertically,
or in both directions. This transform has four straightforward double properties:
. ScaleX—Multiplier for the element’s width (default value = 1)
. ScaleY—Multiplier for the element’s height (default value = 1)
. CenterX—Origin for horizontal scaling (default value = 0)
. CenterY—Origin for vertical scaling (default value = 0)

SkewTransform
SkewTransform slants an element according to the values of four double properties:
. AngleX—Amount of horizontal skew (default value = 0)
. AngleY—Amount of vertical skew (default value = 0)
. CenterX—Origin for horizontal skew (default value = 0)
. CenterY—Origin for vertical skew (default value = 0)

TranslateTransform
TranslateTransform simply moves an element according
to two double properties:
. X—Amount to move horizontally (default value = 0)
. Y—Amount to move vertically (default value = 0)

MatrixTransform
MatrixTransform is a low-level mechanism that can be used to create custom 2D transforms.
MatrixTransform has a single Matrix property (of type
System.Windows.Media.Matrix) representing a 3x3 affine transformation matrix. In case
you’re not a linear algebra buff, this basically means that all the previous transforms (or
any combination of them) can also be expressed using MatrixTransform.
The 3x3 matrix has the following values:
M11 M12 0
M21 M22 0
OffsetX OffsetY 1
The final column’s values are fixed, but the other six values can be set as properties of the
Matrix type (with the same names as shown) or via a constructor that accepts the six
values in row-major order.

3 marks) Explain Grid splitter

Another attractive feature of Grid is its support for interactive resizing of rows and columns
using a mouse or keyboard (or stylus or finger, depending on your hardware). This is
accomplished with the GridSplitter class from the same namespace. You can add any
number of GridSplitter children to a Grid and give them Grid.Row, Grid.Column,
Grid.RowSpan, and/or Grid.ColumnSpan attached property values like any other
children. Dragging a GridSplitter resizes at least one cell. Whether the other cells resize
or simply move depends on whether they use proportional or nonproportional sizing

when we preferred BeginInvoke instead of Invoke method? (2 Marks)
there are times when you want to invoke a delegate and wait for its
execution to complete before the current thread continues. In those
